title: How steep before it slides?
question: If you tilt the slope little by little, at what angle does the box start to slide?
steps: Pick the surface material and set the slope angle.
Press Release box and see whether the box holds.
Near the critical angle, change the angle a little and compare.
observe: See whether the box starts to slide at the moment the part of gravity along the slope gets bigger than the maximum static friction.

terms.name: Static friction
terms.description: The force that holds touching objects so they do not slide.

terms.name: Maximum static friction
terms.description: The biggest friction that can hold an object just before it moves.

terms.name: Kinetic friction
terms.description: The friction that works against a sliding object's motion.

terms.name: Critical angle
terms.description: The smallest tilt at which an object on a slope starts to slide.

law.title: The slope and friction
law.description: When the part of gravity along the slope is bigger than the maximum static friction, the box slides, and while it slides, kinetic friction lowers the acceleration.

tip: Drag the box with one finger to a start place on the slope: it starts sliding from there. Drag with two fingers to turn the view, and spread or pinch them to zoom and move.
tip_short: Drag the box onto the slope and it slides

controls.label: Surface material
controls.note: The box and the slope are of the same material.

predict.question: If you tilt the wooden slide a little, will the box go down?
predict.reason: Even a little tilt lets gravity pull the box hard. Once that is bigger than friction, the box slides down.
predict.bridge: Tilt it, let go and see for yourself!

stages.text: Tilt the wooden slide a little and knock over the yellow dominoes!
stages.say: Gravity pulls the box down, and the floor holds on to it. The floor's holding force is called **friction**. Even a little tilt lets the pull beat friction. So the box slides down.
stages.win: Crash! The yellow dominoes fell over!
stages.miss: Let the box go from the very top!
stages.miss_conditions: Pick Wood and A little tilt!

stages.text: Keep the wood, tilt it more and knock over the blue dominoes!
stages.say: With a bigger tilt, gravity pulls the box down harder. So the box gets faster and goes farther.
stages.win: The blue dominoes fell over too!
stages.miss: Let the box go from the very top!
stages.miss_conditions: Pick Wood and A big tilt!

stages.text: Keep the tilt, switch to steel and knock over the red pillar!
stages.say: Steel is slippery, so its friction is small. So at the same tilt the box goes faster and farther.
stages.win: Boom! The red pillar fell over!
stages.miss: Let the box go from the very top!
stages.miss_conditions: Pick Steel and A big tilt!

story.clue: The piece is on top of the red pillar! Let's knock down the dominoes with the box!

kid.intro: This is the slide lab. Gravity pulls the box down the slide. The floor holds on to the box. The floor's holding force is called **friction**. Change the floor's material and the tilt! Let's see how fast the box goes down.
kid.title: Let's slide a box down the slide!
kid.say: Tilt the slide and the box slides down. The more you tilt, the faster it goes.
kid.tip: Tap the box and it slides down!

note.law: The steeper the slope, the bigger the force pulling the box down, so it gains speed faster as it slides.
note.learn: The steeper the slope, the harder the box is pulled down it. It starts to slide at the angle where that pull beats the grip of the surface, and a slippery surface lets go at a lower angle.
talk: Where on a playground slide do you go fastest?
Why is a slide more slippery after rain?
